content: Orthogonality: Changes to one module should not require changes to another. Minimize coupling between components. Each component should have one axis of change.

metadata.detection: high fan-out, cross-module edits in same commit, shotgun surgery

content: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself): Every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous, authoritative representation within a system.

metadata.detection: duplicate code blocks, duplicated constants, copy-paste patterns

content: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It): Don't build for hypothetical future requirements. Only implement what is needed now.

metadata.detection: unused exports, dead code, speculative abstractions, empty interfaces

content: KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid): Choose the simplest solution that works. Complexity should be justified by real requirements.

metadata.detection: cyclomatic complexity >10, deep nesting >4, long methods >50 lines

content: Separation of Concerns: Each module, class, or function should handle one concern. UI should not contain business logic. Data access should not contain presentation logic.

metadata.detection: god classes, mixed business/UI logic, database queries in views

content: Single Responsibility Principle: A class or module should have one, and only one, reason to change.

metadata.detection: large files >500 lines, multiple concerns per class, many public methods

content: Dependency Inversion Principle: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.

metadata.detection: direct instantiation instead of DI, concrete type imports across layers

content: Open/Closed Principle: Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification. Add new behavior without changing existing code.

metadata.detection: switch statements on types, no protocol/interface, modification required for new variants

content: Liskov Substitution Principle: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of a subclass without breaking the application.

metadata.detection: protocol violations, unexpected behavior in subclasses, type checks on subtypes

content: Interface Segregation Principle: No client should be forced to depend on methods it does not use. Prefer many small interfaces over one large one.

metadata.detection: fat protocols/interfaces, empty method implementations, unused required methods
